guidance: The course is the guide: one path between walls, a start banner and a finish banner; every goal sits on or above it in course order
Landmarks: dam, reservoir, Mountain Dew billboards, generator building, yellow/black hazard rails; the tape branches at the dam
Breadcrumbs on the high road: A over the dam's back quarter pipe, a 500 icon over the natural arch, a darkened strip of worn rock on the arch (G1 p106)
Target in a bowl: the tape glows over yellow rails in the centre of a round canyon, visible across the curved approach (thumbsticks)
Hidden on purpose: the entry is a rail 'that extends back across the path', easy to read as part of the main line; the tape is invisible from the start and the upstream main line
At downhill speed the target is shown late and briefly ('only seconds to make adjustments before the leap', G1 p108), so route knowledge matters
designLogic: Course order is goal order: valves V1-V5 and S-K-A-T-E appear in course order, the letters in spelling order
The tape is a parallel high road branching at the dam (marked by A) and rejoining the main line at valve 4
On a hill speed is free and control is the test: brake, steer after landings, hit a quarter pipe at a shallow angle
No retry within a run: a miss drops the skater below the branch and the hill cannot be climbed back (G1 p099 'You can't fight the hill')
Big catch area at the end: four parallel rails, 'if you hit any of the rails, you're home free' (G1 p107)
The tape's exit lines the skater up with valve 4 (G1 p103): no dead end
The target is shown across a curve: a round canyon keeps it in view along the rim at downhill speed
Worn rock as a path cue, presented as the trace of the developers' own runs (G1 p106)
The expert line is one air: TAS1 clears the high road with one christ air from the dam quarter pipe over the arch (3 s)
Few named gaps: three types in the original; the tape's three gaps are unnamed
Main-line risks (Huge Water Hazard, ski jump) are scored; the tape adds a hidden risk above them
Difficulty peak of the career: G1 calls it 'by far the most challenging' and ranks Streets' tape second to it (G1 p099, p122)
remakeChanges: Tape: same high road; PS12 adds 'the big ramp to get over to the tape, above some rails' for the last gap
Pipe Flip (1000) names the first leg of the high road (left ramp → rail across → next rail → back down)
Letters keep their order; E moves from the generator rail to a quarter pipe after T (PS12)
Valves re-dressed (yellow pipes, big kicker, high pipe, 'KEEP CLEAR' structure, right-hand wall)
New goals: 5 hard hats, Madonna the Huge Water Hazard Gap, Air Walk the Hydrophobic Gap; VV logo placed on the high road
transfer: High road on a one-way course: after a dam halfpipe, branch an elevated path (rail across, second rail back, arch) ≈ 5-10 m above the main line for ≈ 100 m, ending at a crystal over a rail cluster on a pillar; rejoin at the next objective
Control not speed: near 23 m/s make braking and steering the test; rail-to-rail hops within the ≈ 2.4 m grind-ollie pop; a quarter pipe at a shallow angle to carry ≈ 6-8 m
Generous catch: 3-4 parallel rails ≈ 1.5-2 m apart so the 2.1 m grind snap catches any; crystal ≈ 0.5-1 m above the rail line
Target in a bowl: crystal in the centre of a round canyon with the approach along the rim
Breadcrumbs: a floating bonus over the arch and a worn-texture strip; a level collectible at the branch point
Expert shortcut: a big vert air or spine transfer from the dam quarter pipe over the arch onto the podium (≈ 12-14 m)
Cheaper retry than THPS: a rope swing or moving platform from the main line back up to the branch for one retry
openQuestions: Heights of the high road, plateau and podium above the lower path (≈ 4-8 m inferred)
